title: Amazon Cuts Jobs in Its AGI Unit Even as AI Investment Soars
excerpt: The tech giant is trimming roles within its artificial general intelligence division while continuing to pour billions into AI, months after cutting 16,000 jobs company-wide.
body:
• Amazon has eliminated positions in its Artificial General Intelligence division, though it has not disclosed the number of affected employees.
  • The layoffs hit teams led by VPs Adeeb Shanaa and Vishal Sharma, following earlier departures of senior AGI executives Rohit Prasad and David Luan.
  • Affected U.S. workers will receive 90 days of pay and benefits, outplacement support, transitional healthcare coverage, and severance eligibility.

Amazon cut jobs in parts of its artificial general intelligence organization on Wednesday, the latest targeted workforce reduction at the tech giant as it reshapes teams to prioritize projects with the greatest customer impact, Reuters and The Wall Street Journal reported.

The company did not disclose how many employees were affected. The cuts hit teams within the AGI Data Services unit, led by Vice President Adeeb Shanaa, and the AGI Information team, headed by Vice President Vishal Sharma, according to The Bridge Chronicle.

"We've been building large AI models for several years, and it remains one of the most important things we're working on. This is a fast-moving space, and we're sharpening our focus on the initiatives that matter most for customers, so we can move faster on what counts."

— Amazon spokesperson, to Reuters

The spokesperson said that increased focus required "some difficult decisions, including eliminating some roles within parts of our AGI organization," while Amazon continues investing in AI initiatives it considers most important for customers.

A Pattern of Restructuring

The AGI layoffs are the latest in a series of smaller cuts since Amazon eliminated roughly 16,000 jobs across the company in January, as CEO Andy Jassy pushed to streamline operations while accelerating AI investments. The company has been methodically trimming teams even as it ramps up spending on AI infrastructure.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=ctm8zI8RhPs

The AGI division itself has undergone significant reorganization. In December, Amazon placed the unit under Senior Vice President Peter DeSantis alongside its silicon chip and quantum computing teams. The group has also lost senior leadership over the past year, including the departures of executives Rohit Prasad and David Luan, according to multiple reports.

The division works on building large-scale foundation models and developing general-purpose AI systems capable of performing complex tasks autonomously, including tools such as Amazon Nova Act. Amazon continues to develop its Nova family of foundation models and invest heavily in generative AI services for customers through Amazon Web Services.

Big Tech's AI Paradox: Spend More, Cut Staff

Amazon's move mirrors a broader pattern across the technology industry: companies are increasing AI capital expenditure to record levels while simultaneously cutting headcount in teams that don't align with their sharpened strategic priorities. The result is a workforce that is smaller but more concentrated around a handful of high-priority AI bets.

Amazon's stock fell 1.5 percent on the day of the layoffs, dropping for the second consecutive session, according to StockTwits. The cuts come ahead of Amazon's second-quarter earnings report, where investors will be watching closely for signals on how the company's AI spending is translating into revenue.

Affected U.S. employees will receive 90 days of pay and benefits, outplacement support, transitional healthcare benefits, and will be eligible for severance payments, the company said.

What It Means for Indian Tech Workers

Amazon's AGI teams employ a significant number of Indian-origin engineers and executives. VP Vishal Sharma, whose team was directly affected, is among the senior Indian-origin leaders in the division. For Indian tech professionals on H-1B visas working in Amazon's AI units, layoffs carry heightened stakes: the 60-day grace period to find a new employer or change visa status creates urgent pressure that U.S. citizens and permanent residents do not face.

The broader trend of targeted AI restructuring across big tech — with Google, Meta, and Microsoft all undertaking similar moves in recent months — means fewer but more competitive openings in the AI space, even as overall AI investment continues to grow.

What to Watch

Amazon's Q2 earnings report will be closely scrutinized for details on the returns from its AI investments and whether the restructuring is producing the efficiency gains the company is seeking. Investors and employees alike will be watching whether additional cuts follow in other parts of the organization, or whether the AGI trimming marks the end of the post-January reduction cycle.
